definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese sweets with high moisture content, typically made from ingredients like mochi, bean paste, and agar. They are perishable and meant to be eaten soon after purchase.

⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{生菓子|なまがし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦お{茶|ちゃ}→お茶：00576_ocha⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦いただいた→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧。
examples.english: I enjoyed seasonal fresh sweets together with tea.

notes:
A category of traditional Japanese sweets (⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧) characterized by high moisture content (typically over 30%). They are soft and perishable, in contrast to {干菓子|ひがし} (dry confections) which keep much longer. Common types include ⟦{練|ね}り{切|き}り→練り切り：28742_nerikiri⟧ (nerikiri), ⟦{大福|だいふく}→大福：12173_daifuku⟧ (daifuku), and ⟦{羊羹|ようかん}→羊羹：05002_youkan⟧ (yokan).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{生菓子|なまがし} — seasonal fresh sweets
- {上生菓子|じょうなまがし} — premium fresh confections (served at formal tea ceremonies)
- {生菓子|なまがし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧ — to make fresh sweets

CULTURAL NOTE:
Fresh confections are closely tied to the tea ceremony (⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧), where they are served to complement the bitterness of ⟦{抹茶|まっちゃ}→抹茶：10574_maccha⟧. Designs often reflect the current season — cherry blossoms in spring, maple leaves in autumn — making them a form of edible art.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧ — Japanese sweets (broader category that includes both fresh and dry varieties)
- {干菓子|ひがし} — dry Japanese confections (longer shelf life, served at casual tea gatherings)
